meaning: A way to sign in with your phone's fingerprint, face, or screen lock PIN instead of a password.
clues: It is a way to prove who you are when you sign in to an account.
It uses a phone or computer unlock method, such as a fingerprint, face scan, or screen lock PIN.
It uses a pair of digital keys, with one key kept private by your device.
It is made for sites and services that support this sign-in method.
It has seven letters and starts with P.

decoys.meaning: A small physical device you tap or plug in to prove your identity when signing in.
Signing in by showing a body feature, such as a fingerprint or face.
A spare code saved for use when you cannot use your usual sign-in proof.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: On a site that supports it, choose the passkey option and follow the phone's screen lock steps. Someone you trust can help.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: A key worked only when it matched the lock. A passkey works the same way: your device and the site must match before the account opens.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Keep your screen lock private. If a site offers a passkey, read its help page before you set one up.

sources.name: Apple Support, About the security of passkeys
Google Help, Sign in with a passkey

blank.sentence: I signed in without a password. My phone's fingerprint scan unlocked my ___.

why: It lets you skip typing a password by using your phone's own unlock.
short: Sign in with fingerprint, not password

situations.text: A site offers a passkey. Should you read its help page before you set one up?
situations.why: Its help page shows the steps. Keep your screen lock private too.
